groups.title: Vowels & Basic Marks
groups.blurb: The tiny marks that tell your voice what to do on every letter.

items.name: Fathah
items.meaning: A small slanted stroke ABOVE a letter.
items.action: Say a short 'a' for 1 count: بَ = ba.

items.name: Kasrah
items.meaning: A small slanted stroke BELOW a letter.
items.action: Say a short 'i' for 1 count: بِ = bi.

example.note: Bi and mi both carry a kasrah.

items.name: Dammah
items.meaning: A tiny waw-shaped mark ABOVE a letter.
items.action: Say a short 'u' for 1 count: بُ = bu.

example.note: Qu and hu carry a dammah.

items.name: Sukun
items.meaning: A small open-headed circle above a letter. Many printed books use a plain small circle (ـْ).
items.action: No vowel: join the letter to the one before it.

items.name: Shaddah
items.meaning: A tiny w-shaped mark above a letter.
items.action: Double the letter: press, then release into its vowel.

items.name: Fathatan
items.meaning: Two fathahs on the last letter of a noun.
items.action: Say '-an'. When you stop, it becomes a long 'aa'.

items.name: Kasratan
items.meaning: Two kasrahs on the last letter of a noun.
items.action: Say '-in'. It is dropped when you stop.

items.name: Dammatan
items.meaning: Two dammahs on the last letter of a noun.
items.action: Say '-un'. It is dropped when you stop.

example.note: A-ha-dun, but you stop and say 'aḥad'.

groups.title: Madd & Little Letters
groups.blurb: Signs that stretch a sound, skip a letter, or change a noon into a meem.

items.name: Madd sign
items.meaning: A small wavy sign above an alif, waw or yaa.
items.action: Stretch the letter beyond 2 counts. How long depends on the rule (4 to 5 or 6 counts).

example.note: ٱلسَّمَآءُ: the sign tells you to stretch.

items.name: Dagger alif
items.meaning: A tiny upright stroke above a letter.
items.action: Read it as a long 'aa' for 2 counts.

items.name: Small waw
items.meaning: A small waw after the pronoun هُ.
items.action: Stretch 'hu' into 'huu' for 2 counts.

items.name: Small yaa
items.meaning: A small yaa after the pronoun هِ.
items.action: Stretch 'hi' into 'hee' for 2 counts.

items.name: Alif of joining
items.meaning: An alif with a small head on top.
items.action: Say it only when you START on it. Skip it when joined to the previous word.

items.name: Small round zero
items.meaning: A small round zero above a letter.
items.action: The letter is written but not pronounced.

items.name: Small meem (above)
items.meaning: A tiny meem above a noon sakinah or tanween that is followed by ب.
items.action: Iqlab: say a hidden meem and hum for 2 counts.

example.note: Dhambihim: the noon becomes a meem.

items.name: Small meem (below)
items.meaning: A tiny meem under a kasratan that is followed by ب.
items.action: Iqlab: say a hidden meem and hum for 2 counts.

example.note: Shiqaaqin ba'eed: the tanween becomes a meem.

groups.title: Stop Signs
groups.blurb: The little signs above words that tell you when to stop and when to go on.

items.name: Must stop (meem)
items.meaning: A small meem above a word.
items.action: You must stop. Continuing could change the meaning.

items.name: Do not stop (laa)
items.meaning: The word لا (no) above a word.
items.action: Do not stop here. If you must, go back a few words and restart.

items.name: Either is fine (jeem)
items.meaning: A small jeem above a word.
items.action: Stopping and continuing are equally fine.

items.name: Stopping is better (qalaa)
items.meaning: The word قلى above a word.
items.action: Stopping is better than continuing, but you may continue.

items.name: Continuing is better (salaa)
items.meaning: The word صلى above a word.
items.action: Continuing is better than stopping, but you may stop.

items.name: Stop at one of two (three dots)
items.meaning: Three dots appear in two places close to each other.
items.action: Stop at one of the two places, but not both.

example.note: Stop after رَيْبَ or after فِيهِ, not both.

items.name: Short pause (seen)
items.meaning: A small seen above a word.
items.action: Pause briefly without taking a breath.

groups.title: Other Signs
groups.blurb: Markers for the end of a verse, a prostration, and a section of the Quran.

items.name: End of verse
items.meaning: A circle with the verse number inside.
items.action: Marks the end of a verse. It is always a safe place to stop.

items.name: Prostration of recitation
items.meaning: A sign after a verse that mentions prostration.
items.action: Marks a verse where the prostration of recitation (sujood at-tilawah) is made.

example.note: The sajdah sign ends this verse.

items.name: Quarter-hizb marker
items.meaning: A decorative star at the start of a verse.
items.action: Marks the start of a quarter of a hizb, one of the divisions of the Quran.
